data_used.source: Search Console export, Web, last 3 months (2026-08-05 to 2026-11-04): Pages, Queries (top 1,000), Chart, Devices, Countries, Search appearance. Copy at /mnt/project-files/hdr-seo/gsc-export-2026-11-06/.
limits: Queries are not tied to pages in this export; queries were matched to pages by topic.
The top-1,000 queries cover 26,307 of 254,374 impressions (about 10%); the rest is long-tail or anonymized.
The window ends 2026-11-04, before round one went live (2026-11-05), so it is the baseline for round one too.

selection_method: Tips pages at average position 9 or better, ranked by impressions x (1.05% minus current CTR). 1.05% is what phone-screen-black-but-on gets at position 5.4 with a title that mirrors searcher phrasing; it is the realistic ceiling on this site, not an industry curve.
pattern_used: Searcher's exact symptom phrase first, as a question, then one specific promise from the page (a named test, setting or verdict). Titles 49 to 57 characters for mobile (64% of impressions).

pages.selection: Top query cluster is 'how to tell/know if the screen or the protector is cracked' (about 126 queries, 3,579 impressions in the visible sample, mostly position 7.5 to 8.7). Old title led with 'Cracked screen protector', a phrasing almost nobody types. New title puts 'cracked screen' first and names the hope behind the search: that it's only the protector.
pages.note: Also absorbs 'reglass for iphone meaning' (1,136 impressions, 0 clicks, pos 9.7), which the page does not answer; see other_findings.

insights: Click-starved results pages: across the top 1,000 queries, CTR is 2.4% at positions 1-3, 1.3% at 3-5 and 1.1% at 5-8, a fraction of normal curves. Symptom questions get answered on the results page (AI Overviews, featured snippets, People also ask), so title gains have a ceiling near 1%.
About 66% of impressions are outside the US (UK, India, Philippines, Canada, Australia lead). Tips clicks from there build authority but can't become customers; judge business value on US clicks.
Site-wide CTR has been flat around 0.65% while impressions grew from about 23K in August to 138K in October; reach is growing faster than clicks.
other_findings: Local IT queries rank top 3 with zero clicks: 'it experts in hailey' pos 2.0, 'local it support hailey' pos 1.9, 'it solutions near me hailey' pos 3.4, 'data backup and recovery hailey' pos 2.9 (107 imp). The likely landing page (computer-support) is titled 'Computer Help in Hailey, ID', which doesn't say IT support. These are money queries; worth a title and content look (not a tips page, so out of this round).

'reglass for iphone meaning' has 1,136 impressions, 0 clicks: the biggest single zero-click query. No page explains reglass (glass-only screen refurbishing). Candidate for a short tips page or a section on the screen-protector page.
'why does keyboard overheat' (345 imp) and a 218-impression multiple-choice exam-style query about laptop heat suggest a 'why is my laptop keyboard hot' angle worth a section.

Stray URLs with a few impressions, likely invented by AI answers or old links: /tips/phone-screen-black-on, /tips/phone-screen-black-but-still-on-what-to-do-after-a-drop, /tips/cracked-phone-screen-safe-to-use, /tips/screen-protector-or-phone-screen, /tips/lcd-oled, /tips/ps5-not-charging, /tips/iphone-stuck-on-the-apple-logo, /backup-iphone-broken-screen, /tips/iPhone-ghost-touch-cracked-screen. None has a redirect in vercel.json; cheap 301s to the real pages would catch them. Trailing-slash variants (1 to 3 impressions) should already redirect since vercel.json sets trailingSlash false; apex-domain URLs (haileyrepair.com without www) also show single impressions, worth confirming the apex redirects to www in Vercel.
Some impressions come from long exam-style or AI-agent queries ('a customer says that a green line...', 'context: location: germany...'); these never click and slightly depress CTR.
measure: Compare these 10 pages' CTR for matched 28-day windows before and after going live, US and all countries. Expect gains of a few tenths of a point, not a jump to normal-curve CTR.
